record.original_question: Is there a number N such that every irreducible geodesic net whose unbalanced vertices are exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2.3. Is there a number N such that each irreducible geodesic net with unbalanced vertices at all vertices of a regular tetrahedron has at most N balanced vertices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic net in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a finite graph linearly embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose edges are straight line segments. A vertex $v$ of such a net is called balanced if the sum of the unit vectors along the edges emanating from $v$ equals the zero vector; otherwise $v$ is called unbalanced. A geodesic net is called irreducible if it does not contain a proper subgraph that is itself a geodesic net (i.e., one cannot remove any nonempty proper subset of its edges and still leave a geodesic net on a subset of its vertices with the same balanced/unbalanced classification at remaining interior vertices).

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $N$ with the following property? For every irreducible geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose set of unbalanced vertices is exactly the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron, the number of balanced vertices of the net is at most $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question in the plane (four unbalanced/boundary points) appears to remain open, with recent work (2024–2025) constructing irreducible planar geodesic nets with four boundary vertices and increasing numbers of balanced vertices (e.g., 16, then 25), suggesting the bound may not exist. For the three-dimensional regular tetrahedron version specifically, no resolution has been located in the literature, and it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: construction of an irreducible geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices, increasing the previously known maximum from 16 to 25
status_evidence.claim: Recent work indicates the analogous problem with four boundary vertices remains open with constructions giving ever larger numbers of balanced vertices.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets with Few Boundary Points (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: discussion of irreducible geodesic nets and bounds on balanced vertices given few boundary points
status_evidence.claim: The bound problem for four boundary points (including tetrahedron configurations) is discussed as an open question.
